analysis.title: Iran War Chartpack Week 33: Dances With Snakes
key_insights: SEB sees the current Middle East equilibrium as inherently unstable absent a diplomatic breakthrough. Iran has shown it can withstand the US naval blockade for several months, and some analysts think the US Navy may have under six months to hold an effective blockade.
Roughly 40% of Middle East crude exports now use Strait of Hormuz (SoH) bypass mechanisms. Non-Iranian Middle East oil exports have picked up, but at higher transport costs.

Iranian tanker attacks are more numerous and severe and may intensify ahead of the US midterms. SEB expects a volatile October, with fears of renewed US attacks after the midterms and Iranian retaliation or preemption.

Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure show vulnerabilities beyond tanker transit. The report lists 15-20 attack waves on six of seven days, hits on King Khalid International Airport, an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran targeted on Oct 13, and a Saudi air defense failure over 1,000 km.

Saudi Arabia struck Houthi oil and fuel storage on Oct 13 (Ras Isa, Hodeidah), and the Houthis and Saudis each declared oil sites legitimate targets. The Houthis also declared a blockade on Saudi-linked vessels, which makes Bab al-Mandeb a second chokepoint and exposes the SoH workaround.

Trump has three options: continue the blockade, accept Iranian demands and reopen the SoH, or intensify the war. SEB says each carries a strategic or domestic political cost, and that US acquiescence is unlikely given domestic costs.
Israel's Oct 27 election creates escalation incentives. Israel's focus has shifted to Lebanon, with indefinite occupation of a security zone and diplomacy aimed at dissolving Hezbollah.

SEB's scenario table gives a probability-weighted 3-month Brent of $97.0/b against a current futures price of $100.6/b. Probabilities: renewed conflict 30% ($100-150), negotiations 40%, Iran capitulation 5%, low-intensity unfinished conflict 20% ($80-100), regime destabilization 5% ($90-100). Prolonged conflict totals 55%.
Prediction markets show low expectations of SoH reopening. The 60-transit-call threshold used is only about two-thirds of the 2025 average transit count (IMF PortWatch).

The gasoil-Brent crack spread rose from about $27/bbl at the start of 2025 to a peak of $101/bbl in September. Drivers are Iran War disruption, Ukrainian strikes cutting Russian diesel exports, limited European refining capacity and seasonal demand.

EIA expects Brent to average about $90/b in 2H26 and $74/b in 2027. Regional shut-ins averaged 6.7m b/d in July, global inventories fell 4.2m b/d in 2Q26 and are forecast to fall 3.8m b/d in 3Q26, and most shut-in output is restored in mid-2027.
Physical and paper oil prices diverge. Sticky longer-dated DFL spreads indicate the market is pricing supply pressure into 2027.
Iran has an estimated 20-35mb of crude storage left, about 2-3 weeks before forced production cuts. Losing close to 1.6m b/d of exports would strain Iran's external balance.
Iran's economy is under severe strain: July headline inflation of 88% (food 128%), an eighth currency crisis since 2016, and about 10-12 million jobs at risk.

The US is leaning on economic measures (targeting Chinese banks, yuan oil payments, Hong Kong intermediaries) because of munitions depletion and reduced Gulf base presence. CSIS estimates Tomahawk and THAAD stocks take 3+ years to rebuild.

SEB flags Arab intelligence reports of an Iranian shift toward offensive deterrence. Possible actions include sabotage of Gulf internet cables, unrest in Kuwait and Bahrain, and strikes on US bases in Europe.
The IMF October 2026 WEO shows large downward GDP revisions for MENA and EM. Sovereign CDS spreads are rising again, and energy inflation rates have risen in many countries since February.

sector_views.rationale: Scenario-weighted Brent of $97 sits below the $100.6 futures price. The curve prices supply pressure into 2027, and 55% of the scenario weight is prolonged conflict.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The market price sits above SEB's scenario-weighted $97.0/b, so the futures price embeds more risk premium than SEB's probabilities imply.
A probability-weighted average of scenario mid-ranges, not a forecast. Renewed conflict is the upside tail at $100-150.
EIA expects prices to ease as production rises and inventories rebuild.
2Q26 is an EIA estimate and 3Q26 is its forecast. Continued stock draws support prices.
Diesel is very tight relative to crude, which signals product-market stress beyond crude.
Record inflation shows mounting economic pressure from the blockade and war damage.

risk_factors: Renewed US-Iran war, which SEB weights at 30% with Brent at $100-150.
Escalation of the Houthi-Saudi conflict to Gulf energy infrastructure, aviation and undersea cables.
The US naval blockade may be unsustainable beyond about six months.
An Iranian preemptive offensive, including attacks on US bases in Europe and Gulf infrastructure sabotage.
Depleted interceptor and munitions stocks limit US and allied defensive capacity.
Rising sovereign credit risk, supply chain disruption and cost-push inflation.
charts_described: Prediction-market chart: expectations of SoH reopening remain low, with the 60-transit-call threshold at about two-thirds of the 2025 average.
Table of munitions use in the Iran War and estimated return to prewar inventory, from Tomahawk (late 2030 to early 2031) to PrSM (late 2026).
vol_and_positioning: SEB expects a volatile October driven by escalation risk around the US midterms and the Israeli election.

tension_points.bull_case: Continued blockade deepens Iran's economic crisis (88% inflation, storage nearly full) and may bring concessions, with a skinny deal as SEB's base case.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran has shown it can endure for months, may prefer resuming war to waiting, and the US may have under six months to sustain the blockade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A diplomatic breakthrough, or an Iranian preemptive offensive that ends the blockade standoff.

theme_stances.key_argument: Absent a diplomatic breakthrough the equilibrium is unstable and the road to intensified conflict remains open.
theme_stances.evidence: the prevailing geopolitical equilibrium in the Middle East is inherently unstable

theme_stances.key_argument: Explicit threats to oil sites raise the oil risk premium.
theme_stances.evidence: the explicit threats to oil sites raise the risk premium
